name: Van Cortlandt Golf Course
note: The oldest public golf course in the United States: 'established in 1895 as a nine-hole course and expanded to eighteen holes in 1899' (opened 6 July 1895). Point: the holes north of the lake (OSM outlines 'Van Cortlandt Golf Course' and its unnamed duplicate).

name: Van Cortlandt Golf Course
note: Same course: the four holes south of Van Cortlandt Lake (unnamed OSM outlines that also take in Mosholu); the 1899 enlargement to 18 holes is not separated (estimated).

name: Mosholu Golf Course
note: Nine-hole course in the south-east corner of Van Cortlandt Park, 'built in 1914'. OSM maps it without a name; the point is inside its outline.

name: Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Course
note: 'The Pelham Bay Golf Course opened in 1901, followed by the Split Rock Golf Course in 1935.' One OSM outline for both: features take the year of the nearer point. Pelham Bay course = the eastern half toward Shore Road (position of the split ESTIMATED).

name: Pelham Bay & Split Rock Golf Course
note: Split Rock Golf Course, John van Kleek, opened June 1935 with the rebuilt Pelham course ('The golf courses were reopened in June 1935'): the western half toward the Hutchinson River marshes and Split Rock (position of the split ESTIMATED).

name: Forest Park Golf Course
note: 'A nine-hole golf course opened in 1901 ... a clubhouse and another nine holes were added in 1905.' The 1905 holes are not separated (estimated).

name: Dyker Beach Golf Course
note: ESTIMATED. Golf on the Dyker Meadow from the late 1890s: the Dyker Meadow company 'leased the land to both the Dyker Golf Club and Marine and Field Club, who used the Dyker Heights Club House, built in 1898, as their golf club house'; 'second oldest in New York City, behind Van Cortlandt'. The city course took its present extent with the parcels of 1924-27 and 1934 and the fill begun in 1918: later holes are not separated.

name: Richmond County Country Club
note: Club founded 1888, golf from 1894; 'In 1897, RCCC moved to its present location in Dongan Hills'.

name: Towers Country Club
note: Unnamed in OSM (the course around North Shore Towers, Glen Oaks). 'In 1923, the Glen Oaks Golf Club was built'; the towers replaced part of the course by 1971 and the remaining holes were rearranged: today's layout is younger than 1923 (ESTIMATED).

name: Clearview Park
note: Clearview Park Golf Course (OSM name 'Clearview Park'): opened 1925 as the private Clearview Golf and Yacht Club (Willie Tucker); bought by the city 25 June 1931 (NYC Parks, read through a search result: the site refuses automated requests).

name: South Shore Golf Course
note: 'South Shore Golf Course, built in 1927' (Staten Island Chamber of Commerce) as a private country club; city course later. Other listings say 1929.

name: Douglaston Golf Course
note: ESTIMATED. Built as the North Hills Country Club, designed by Willie Tucker in 1925 (Bayside Historical Society); the opening year 1927 is not verified in a source read here. City course since the early 1960s (Parks acquisition date 7 Sep 1962).

name: Silver Lake Golf Course
note: 'In 1928 the land was converted to a golf course ... The golf course itself was completed in 1929' (on the former Marine Cemetery).

name: La Tourette Golf Course
note: 'The first nine holes, designed by David L. Rees, opened in 1929. In 1935, John Van Kleek designed nine new holes and redesigned the original nine.' The 1935 holes are not separated (estimated).

name: Kissena Golf Course
note: 'Designed by John Van Kleek, the Kissena Park golf course opened in 1935' (NYSGA; some listings say 1934).

name: Jacob Riis Park Golf Course
note: 'The park's pitch and putt golf course was opened on May 14, 1938.'

name: Alley Pond Golf Center
note: ESTIMATED: driving range east of the Northern Boulevard bridge over Alley Creek; 'The golf center has operated since the 1950s'.

name: Marine Park Golf Course
note: 'The 210-acre golf course opened in 1963' (Robert Trent Jones, on Jamaica Bay fill).

name: Flushing Meadows Golf Center
note: ESTIMATED: pitch-and-putt and miniature golf at the north end of Meadow Lake, on 1964-65 World's Fair ground; dated to the park's return to the city in June 1967. The centre's own opening year was not found.

name: Bally's Golf Links at Ferry Point
note: Jack Nicklaus course on the former landfill: 'the golf course, which opened in 2015' (as Trump Golf Links at Ferry Point; renamed 2023).
